newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian concern over jobs hits 10-year high.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian concern over jobs hits 10-year high.

text.p: Brazilians are more worried about unemployment than at any other time in the last ten years, a poll published on Friday said.

Fifty-nine percent of 2,000 people interviewed between November 27 and December 1 cited unemployment as their biggest concern, up from 54 percent in March 1995, said the National Industry Confederation (CNI), which commissioned the survey.

Brazil's official unemployment rate fell to 4.56 percent in November, down from 5.14 percent in October, the government's National Statistics Institute said on Friday. But trade unions in Sao Paulo say the real rate there is closer to 15 percent.

The poll, by the independent Brazilian Public Opinion Institute (Ibope), found a clear link between income and fear of unemployment -- 74 percent of workers earning one minimum salary of 112 reais a month said they were worried about it, compared with 52 percent of workers who finished secondary school.

The percentage of those worried about the spending power of their salaries fell to 28 percent from 35 percent in March 1995, reflecting real increases in the value of salaries and higher anxiety about hanging on to jobs, the CNI said.
Forty-five percent cited the state of Brazil's ailing public health service and 35 percent said they were concerned about drugs.

Corruption was mentioned by only 10 percent of respondents, compared with 30 percent in the end of the 1980s, and only six percent said they were worried about inflation, down from 12 percent in March 1995 and 41 percent in 1994, the CNI said.
Other pressing issues included the quality of public education, cited by 25 percent of those interviewed, the plight of street children at 24 percent and crime with 20 percent.
